subject.title: fix(line): AI-assisted - requireMention can now optionally gate non-text messages with bounded pending-media retention

question: Should LINE support opt-in cross-message media retention through requireMentionForNonText and pendingMediaLimit after the default-path serialization defect is repaired?
rationale: The code can mechanically preserve existing scheduling, but whether OpenClaw should expose two new settings and attach retained media to a later user's mentioned turn is a product and privacy-association choice that tests cannot decide.

options.title: Accept opt-in retention
options.body: Keep both settings, repair default-path locking, document the in-memory delayed-delivery semantics, and require redacted live LINE proof before merge.

options.title: Gate without retention
options.body: Keep only opt-in non-text mention gating and intentionally drop skipped media rather than maintaining cross-message state.

options.title: Decline the feature
options.body: Close this PR and the paired feature issue if delayed media association is not an intended LINE behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept opt-in retention
recommendation.body: Keep both settings, repair default-path locking, document the in-memory delayed-delivery semantics, and require redacted live LINE proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and repaired the prior LINE requireMention implementation, providing the strongest history-based ownership signal for this extension of its semantics.
